This year alone, I have recovered 12 weed wackers including a couple of commercial grade ones, a push mower, and a monster of a chainsaw. All but a few of the weedwackers literally needed about 20 minutes work or less to get running again. I ask that any of you here considering kicking equipment that isn't running to the curb check a few things before you write it off:

Drain the carburetor; this is the most common issue, water settles in the carb over winter and gums it up. Simply dump fresh gas into the tank, and open the carburetors drain cock or screw (its on the bottom usually a 12 mm bolt) and let it drain for about 10 seconds. Engine will almost always start after a pull or two after this fix.

Spark check: This one is very easy and literally only needs a screwdriver. Simply pull the sparkplug wire, stick the screwdriver in the end of the wire, and while hanging on to both and resting your arm on the engine, lightly pull start it. You should feel a small jolt go down your hand that feels like a static shock, this tells you the engine has spark.

If its been setting for years a lot of time it will be seized (cant even draw the pullstarter). Its a simple matter of unscrewing the cylinder head, spraying the cylinder with penetrating oil, then after 5 minutes sticking a piece of wood in there and thwacking it with a mallet. Check to make sure the valves (4 stroke only) move by pullstarting it with the head off, then reassemble. Clean the carburetor listed above and check for spark.

Most older and small engines can be fixed with a combo of the three above, barring the occasional oddball issue which in that case parts cost comes into equation if you want to fix it or not.
